articles.title: A Pennsylvania couple bought 78.3 acres in 2022 to stop development; their conservation work has helped eliminate plans for 88 houses and 21 condos
articles.summary: US News: Paul and Cynthia Black purchased 78.3 acres in Pennsylvania in 2022 with a goal beyond simply owning land that they wanted to ensure it would never be.
articles.body: Paul and Cynthia Black purchased 78.3 acres in Pennsylvania in 2022 with a goal beyond simply owning land that they wanted to ensure it would never be developed. Their latest conservation effort has now permanently protected the property, expanding a 236-acre corridor of preserved land and eliminating plans for 88 houses and 21 condominiums through three contiguous land projects.French & Pickering Creeks Conservation Trust announced the permanent protection of the 78.3-acre property in West Vincent Township on August 13, 2026. The conservation easement was finalized in partnership with the Blacks, West Vincent Township and Chester County, according to a press release published by Phoenixville Regional Chamber of Commerce on their official website.The newly protected land expands an existing cluster of preserved properties, creating a contiguous 236-acre corridor that will remain protected in perpetuity.“This is the third project I have had the honor of working on with Paul and Cynthia Black,” said Pam Brown, Senior Conservation Advisor. “They are true conservation heroes for choosing to protect their land from development.”The property had long been viewed as a prime target for development because of its size and location. It was also the largest unprotected parcel along Pughtown Road, making its preservation a long-standing priority for French & Pickering and West Vincent Township’s Open Space Committee.Couple bought the property with preservation in mindThe effort to protect the land had been more than two decades in the making, but the possibility of preservation gained new momentum when Paul and Cynthia Black purchased the property in 2022.Paul Black said the couple had moved to West Vincent Township in 2015 without initially realizing that the area was facing significant development pressure.“We moved to West Vincent Township in 2015 without realizing that we were moving into the middle of an area that was primed for development,” he said.Since then, the couple have been involved in multiple conservation projects in the area.“In the decade since then, the 1,500+ acre Bryn Coed estate has been preserved and three contiguous land projects that we have been involved in have eliminated plans for 88 houses and 21 condominiums respectively,” Black said.He added that the land will now remain forest and farmland permanently.“It will remain in woods and farmland now forever, a striking contrast to what could have been. French & Pickering were partners for all of it,” he said.Farmland, woodland and a stream will remain protectedThe newly preserved property consists largely of sustainable agricultural farmland, along with woodland and a small stream passage.The land now sits alongside other conservation easements managed by French & Pickering and is located close to Natural Lands’ Bryn Coed Preserve, further expanding the connected landscape of protected land in the region.West Vincent Township officials said the project reflects the community’s long-standing priority of preserving open space and maintaining the area’s rural character.“Our township values open space protection as a very high priority,” said Dana Alan, Chair of the West Vincent Township Board of Supervisors.The township board unanimously voted to use dedicated open-space funds to help complete the project.“Saving open space cannot happen without landowners who love their property and willingly take action to preserve it for the future,” Alan added, praising the Blacks for helping protect the township’s farmland, woodland, vistas and natural resources.$917,000 in grant funding helped complete the dealThe conservation easement was finalized with $917,000 in grant funding from West Vincent Township and Chester County, along with a donation of value from Paul and Cynthia Black.The project builds on a long-standing partnership between French & Pickering, West Vincent Township and Chester County to preserve open space and protect the region’s rural landscape.French & Pickering Executive Director Bill Gladden said the Blacks’ involvement has had a lasting effect on the future of the area.“Paul and Cynthia Black have been extraordinary partners in conservation,” Gladden said. “Their commitment has reshaped the future of this part of West Vincent—replacing development pressure with permanently protected farmland, forest, and clean water.”He added that the project demonstrates how local landowners, government bodies and conservation organisations can work together to preserve land for future generations.“This project reflects the very best of community-driven conservation,” Gladden said, “and French & Pickering is honored to help safeguard a landscape that will benefit residents for generations.”Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Meet Bradley Carlisle, the first professional Santa Claus with Down syndrome in the US: This suburban Atlanta man feared Santa as a child, and now he is honoured by the International Santa Claus Hall of Fame
articles.summary: US News: Bradley Carlisle, a 37-year-old community theatre actor from suburban Atlanta, has become the first professional Santa Claus in the US with Down syndr.
articles.body: Bradley Carlisle, a 37-year-old community theatre actor from suburban Atlanta, has become the first professional Santa Claus in the US with Down syndrome. He was also inducted as an honorary member of the International Santa Claus Hall of Fame after completing one of the largest Christmas performer schools in the US in late August. From fearing Santa Claus to embodying him is less a redemption arc and more a reminder about who gets to see themselves in the stories we tell!He feared Santa as a childBradley Carlisle spent most of his childhood terrified of Santa Claus, according to his mother, Debbie Chadrix, The Guardian reported. He feared St Nick’s white gloves and equated them with the gloves worn by healthcare workers. The medical experiences were difficult for him, and white gloves only meant pain. So when Christmas came around, there was no sitting on Santa's lap, no whispered wishes, no magic.It started in 2023 when Carlisle's mother attended a holiday party thrown by the Down Syndrome Association of Atlanta (DSAA). That’s when the organisation's executive director pulled her aside and said, “We need a Santa with Down syndrome who looks like the kids.”The group’s leader wanted to see if Carlisle would be interested, as they knew his passion for acting. However, she wasn’t sure because she knew her child was terrified of Santa Claus. But she accepted the offer and decided to give it a try. That December, he put on the red suit and showed up. There were more than 200 children.Chadrix can never forget the look on the faces of the children “when they realised Bradley looked like them – and talked like them, a little bit, too”. That’s exactly when Carlisle decided he wanted to be a Santa from then on.By his second Christmas season, the local media picked up Carlisle’s story. His popularity grew. A podcast appearance led to an invitation from Rick Rosenthal, who runs Atlanta's Northern Lights Santa Academy. Rosenthal saw something that others didn’t. It is the second-largest academy of its kind in the US, where actors train to play Santa, Mrs Claus and Christmas elves. When Carlisle arrived at the academy in late August, he trained alongside every other student in the programme. He received no special treatment. At the academy, he learned how to maintain his beard, dress the part and handle the impossible questions kids ask. He excelled in everything.On the academy's final day, Carlisle received word of his induction into the International Santa Claus Hall of Fame. Phil Wenz, representing the Santa Claus Oath Foundation, called him to the stage. Carlisle was appreciated for his confident style while personifying Santa Claus. When Carlisle held up the badge, smiling as the audience applauded, it sent a message to the families watching: their kids can do anything. They can even be Santa! Members of the broader Santa community had pooled resources to create a custom-made suit just for him. His photograph will appear in Times Square as part of Down Syndrome Awareness Month, which starts on his birthday, October 1.Carlisle was honoured not just because he has Down syndrome, but because he is a talented Santa who can connect with people with Down syndrome in a way many other Santas may not be able to. And that’s really important. Because on a December evening, a child with Down syndrome will see a Santa who understands them in a way most Santas cannot.When the academy shared plans to welcome Carlisle to the International Santa Claus Hall of Fame, she had one request. She didn't want her son's condition to be the only reason for the honour. She wanted it to be clear that he had earned this place on his merits.“Phil Wenz knows what he’s looking at. And as soon as he saw Bradley as Santa and talking to people and interacting, he knew he had something different and special – and that’s why he got to the Hall of Fame,” she recalled.Down syndrome is part of the story, but not the entire story.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Explosion of fireworks in central Mexico kills at least 10 dead, injures 64 people
articles.summary: Pyrotechnic material exploded during the festival for a patron saint in a town in Mexico State, collapsing a wall, killing at least 10 people and injuring an...
articles.body:
TEMASCALCINGO, Mexico (AP) — Pyrotechnic material exploded during the festival for a patron saint in a town in Mexico State, collapsing a wall, killing at least 10 people and injuring another 64, Mexican authorities said.

The explosion occurred Saturday night next to the Nuestra Señora de la Luz church in Temascalcingo, a municipality in central Mexico with 66,000 residents. Hundreds of them were preparing to watch a fireworks display that is part of a religious festival when the blast occurred.

The municipality is about 160 kilometers (100 miles) northwest of Mexico City.

The cause of the explosion has not been determined and the Mexico State Attorney General's Office has opened an investigation.

A local bishop said two priests are among the injured.

A video on social media shows the aftermath of the blast, with dozens of people walking through smoke and debris in search of survivors.

Explosions involving pyrotechnics are common in Mexico, where fireworks are frequently used in street celebrations and religious festivals. Almost four years ago, a powerful fireworks explosion in a village in the municipality of Huejutla, in the central state of Hidalgo, left 17 people injured.

articles.title: Isro will never be privatised, its role won't be diminished: Space Agency & INSPACe chief
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Allaying fears of some of its staff that the organisation will be privatised and its role  reduced to an R&D lab, Isro on Sunday dismis.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Allaying fears of some of its staff that the organisation will be privatised and its role reduced to an R&D lab, Isro on Sunday dismissed “speculations and misinformation” about any diminution of its role, calling such reports “baseless and incorrect”. “We wish to categorically state that Isro will neither be privatised nor will its importance be diminished,” the space agency said.Isro further said it “will continue to remain India’s principal institution for advanced space research and technology development, national and strategic missions, space science and exploration, and critical and frontier space capabilities”.Space promoter and regulator Indian National Space Promotion and Authorisation Centre (INSPACe) chairman Pawan Goenka also said on Sunday that Isro “will remain the bedrock of Indian space sector” and it will remain at the core of India’s space programme leading frontier research and the next generation of national space programmes like space station and crewed lunar mission.In a long statement, the space agency said, “Participation of the private sector in space is not about reducing its role. It is about enabling Isro to focus even more strongly on the next generation of India’s space programme, while industry scales mature technologies and capabilities. What is changing is not the importance of Isro, but the scale and structure of India’s space ecosystem.”“The transition is therefore towards an Isro-led national space ecosystem,” the agency said.The agency also said that its “role will progressively strengthen in areas where its scientific expertise matters most: frontier R&D, advanced technologies, human spaceflight, next-generation launch systems, deep-space and planetary missions and strategic national capabilities. It will continue developing cutting-edge technologies, including advanced payloads for communication, navigation and Earth observation, sensors, propulsion systems and other critical technologies.”After nine Isro employee associations have sought a “written clarity” from the agency chairman on the private sector shift, Goenka in a post on X late on Sunday evening said, “Let me say it unequivocally: Isro' s role is by no means diminishing. It will remain the bedrock of the Indian space sector.On scaling up the production of rockets and satellites in India, the INSPACe director declared that the country has set an “ambitious target of 50 launches a year by 2030”. “A goal of this scale cannot be achieved by one organisation alone. Govt and private industry have to build this future together,” he said.Explaining the reasons for opening up the sector, the INSPACe chairman said, Goenka said, “The reforms since 2020 are about expanding India’s overall space ecosystem. IN-SPACe will facilitate and authorise greater non-govt participation, while NSIL will help commercialise mature capabilities.”He said the idea of space reforms is to “let industry increasingly manufacture and scale mature launch vehicles, satellites and other systems, while Isro focuses on what it is uniquely placed to do: advanced R&D, scientific missions, strategic missions, new technologies, and infrastructure that is too complex for the private sector to develop on its own”.Assuring Isro staff that they are going to handle big projects and responsibilities, Goenka said, “Isro will remain at the core of India’s space programme leading frontier research and the next generation of national missions, including the Bharatiya Antariksh Station by 2035, an Indian crewed mission to the Moon by 2040, next-generation launch systems, and sustained lunar and planetary exploration.” Goenka said, “The direction is not a smaller Isro. It is a larger Indian space ecosystem, with Isro pushing the technological frontier.Congratulating Isro for the recent GSLV MK II successful launch, Goenka, in a post on X on Sunday said, “EOS-05 is a major achievement by Isro, and this is just the beginning.”On the growing space sector in the country, the INSPACe regulator said, “From barely a handful of space startups five years ago, India today has over 450. Indian private industry has already flown a rocket to orbit (while referring to Skyroot’s Vikram-1 rocket’s successful launch on July 18). Isro’s research will continue to push the frontiers of what is possible. Private industry must translate that momentum into manufacturing at scale: more rockets, more satellites, more launch capacity and new technologies. That is how we will build a complete space ecosystem and create the capacity to match our ambition.”He said the “opportunity before us is immense: build in India, launch from India and serve the world from India. We are well on our way to taking India’s space sector to a new orbit, figuratively and literally.”Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: IJustLovePuzzles reveals ‘five’ attempts to end her life, says financial stress worsened her struggles while helping daughter
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Twitch streamer IJustLovePuzzles, also known as Gma, has spoken publicly about her past suicide attempts and the financial pressure that made her ment.
articles.body: Twitch streamer IJustLovePuzzles, also known as Gma, has spoken publicly about her past suicide attempts and the financial pressure that made her mental health struggles harder to manage. In a post on X on September 6, 2026, she said she had attempted suicide five times and needed a full year to recover from her most recent attempt. She also explained that financial stress was a major part of those crises. Her comments came shortly after she started a GoFundMe campaign seeking financial help for her daughter, who she says is dealing with serious emotional and financial problems.IJustLovePuzzles says financial stress played a major role in her suicide attemptsIJustLovePuzzles, who has built her Twitch community around solving jigsaw puzzles, said her previous suicide attempts were not caused by one issue alone. She explained that mental health problems and financial pressure often came together.She wrote on X:“I attempted suicide five times. It took me a full year to recover from my last attempt. I was told it's a miracle I survived. Not one time was it because of Major Depression or flashbacks from PTSD alone. It was always a combination of one of those plus financial stress. My older sister cleared all my debt and paid six months' mortgage and utilities so I could focus solely on therapy and healing from my trauma. That's controlling what you can look like when you want someone you care about to live. Feeling hopeless and helpless will drive you to your death.”Her comments give more context to the fundraising campaign she created for her daughter. IJustLovePuzzles said she recognized some of the same pressure in her daughter's situation and wanted to help before it became worse.IJustLovePuzzles was also recognized at both major creator events this year. She received the Heart of the Community award at Streamer University 2026, while her Twitch profile notes that she won the Hidden Gem award at the 2025 Streamer Awards.IJustLovePuzzles asks for help as daughter faces financial and emotional problemsOn September 5, IJustLovePuzzles launched a GoFundMe titled “Help me save my daughters life.” The fundraiser says her daughter is facing financial pressure and emotional strain after leaving what she described as a toxic situation.According to the campaign, her daughter's health insurance stopped, leaving her unable to see her therapist and without medication. IJustLovePuzzles also said her daughter had to leave her apartment early and was being asked to make payments immediately. She added that her daughter did not have a place to stay and had been sleeping without a bed for a month.She also described problems with her daughter's car, saying its air conditioning was not working while she was commuting about an hour to work in the heat.She wrote:“Help me save my daughter's life! articles.summary: Ryan Bridge faces a string of charges including racially aggravated harassment, threats and assault.
articles.body:
The founder of an activist group which has been putting Union Jack and St George's Cross flags on lampposts has been charged with a string of offences including racially aggravated harassment, threatening behaviour and assault.

Ryan Bridge, 45, of Blackwell, Bromsgrove, Worcestershire, has been erecting flags in the Midlands and the south of England since last summer as part of Raise the Colours.

Thames Valley Police said Bridge had been charged with 14 offences from a two-month period in Oxfordshire earlier this year.

He is due to appear at Oxford Magistrates' Court on 3 November.

Seven counts of using threatening words or behaviour to cause harassment, alarm or distress

Three counts of using threatening, abusive or insulting words or behaviour with intent to cause fear of, or provoke, unlawful violence

Two counts of racially aggravated intentional harassment, alarm or distress

One count of racially aggravated fear of violence

In July, Oxfordshire County Council was granted a High Court injunction to stop people placing flags near highways because of safety concerns, trespass and obstruction.

Birmingham City Council has applied for a similar injunction which will be heard at the High Court on Tuesday.

articles.title: How a booming coastal escape learned to coexist with the ocean’s top predator
articles.summary: Cape Cod's tourism economy surged to nearly $2.8 billion as great white sharks fuel a booming ecotourism industry with charter trips and citizen science.
articles.body: As great white sharks increasingly frequent the waters off one popular seaside destination, tourists are flocking there, too — but they’re experiencing the hot spot in a different way. Cape Cod is a renowned seaside destination in southeastern Massachusetts that has long drawn summer vacationers with its picturesque beaches, historic coastal towns and lighthouses. In recent years, though, it has also become increasingly known for its seasonal population of great white sharks. Far from deterring visitors, the presence of sharks is helping fuel a whole new type of tourism. SHARK WEEK ADVISORY AS WARMING SEAS PUSH BLACKTIPS FARTHER NORTH ALONG EAST COAST The New York Times reported that Cape Cod’s tourism economy has grown from nearly $2 billion in 2019 to almost $2.8 billion, according to the Cape Cod Chamber of Commerce. At the same time, the National Park Service has recorded fewer recreational visits to Cape Cod National Seashore, the 40-mile stretch of coastline where white sharks are regularly detected. Shark warning signs and "Stop the Bleed" rescue kits are now fixtures on the beaches. The Atlantic White Shark Conservancy created and runs Sharktivity, a shark-sighting and resource app designed to keep beachgoers apprised of the sharks’ presence. It features alerts for confirmed white shark sightings close to public beaches, along with other shark-safety information. The increased presence of great white sharks in Cape Cod’s waters has been linked to the recovery of the Cape’s gray seal population following the passage of the Marine Mammal Protection Act of 1972. The seal population grew from around 2,000 in 1994 to between 30,000 and 50,000 in 2017, the Times reported. CLICK HERE TO SIGN UP FOR OUR LIFESTYLE NEWSLETTER A 2023 study published in the peer-reviewed journal Marine Ecology Progress Series estimated that roughly 800 individual white sharks visited the waters off Cape Cod between 2015 and 2018, making the area one of the world’s larger white shark hot spots. Despite their growing presence, there is no evidence Cape Cod’s white sharks have become more aggressive or changed their behavior by hunting closer to shore, according to the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy. The sharks have hunted seals in shallow coastal waters since they began predictably returning to the area during the summer and fall. "Sharks have changed behaviors and conversations more than they’ve changed demand," Paul Bordé, a local real estate agent, told the Times. When life gives your town sharks, make shark-spotting profitable. Cape Cod is a rising "white shark ecotourism destination," according to the Times. Shark seekers can hire a private charter through the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy for $2,500 or join an open-boat charter for $500 per person. The 2½-hour trips use spotter pilots to locate sharks, and private charters can book up weeks or even a month in advance, according to the conservancy. CLICK HERE FOR MORE LIFESTYLE NEWS The excursions aren’t purely sightseeing trips. Guests can participate in citizen science by logging shark sightings, using a hydrophone to detect tagged sharks and recording observations that contribute to ongoing research. Because the trips directly support white shark research, a portion of the trip fee is tax-deductible, the conservancy writes on its website. "The fact that we can go out and see them in a two-and-a-half-hour charter is incredibly unique," Hannah Leary, ecotourism coordinator for the Atlantic White Shark Conservancy, told the Times. "We can just come out of the inlet and they’re all right there." The shark presence may also be benefiting some swimming pool companies. Demand for pools has "spiked," the Times reported, and "one Cape Cod pool builder even advertises ‘shark free swimming’ on its trucks." TEST YOURSELF WITH OUR LATEST LIFESTYLE QUIZ The great white sharks’ presence has not been all adventurous sightseeing and tourism dollars, however. A bodysurfer was bitten by a white shark in the area in 2012, and a swimmer was bitten in 2018. Both survived, but later in 2018, Massachusetts recorded its first fatal shark attack since 1936 when a white shark killed a 26-year-old boogie boarder. "I understand the fear," Philadelphia resident Lisa DonDiego told the Times. "And at the end of the day, I recognize that the ocean belongs to them. But I still want to come to Cape Cod." The National Park Service urges beachgoers to stay away from seals and schools of fish, swim in groups and avoid murky or low-visibility water. Purple shark flags at National Seashore beaches indicate that there has been a shark sighting, and swimmers are urged to follow all posted warnings and lifeguard instructions. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP White shark activity also extends beyond Cape Cod’s peak summer season. The National Park Service warns that the predators remain active in the fall, even after seasonal lifeguard coverage ends at National Seashore beaches.

articles.title: More funding needed to boost construction jobs for young people - housing boss
articles.summary: Recent analysis showed the construction sector needs an extra 2,200 workers a year to meet demand.
articles.body:
A long-term plan and additional funding is needed to create more placements for young people within the construction industry, according to one housing association boss.

Iwan Trefor Jones, chief executive at Adra, said it was important that organisations worked together to make sure "that there are opportunities for young people".

Adra had seen a rise in demand in its academy scheme, with one of their recent openings attracting 108 applicants for only six positions.

The Welsh government said work was already under way "to boost construction skills" and new apprenticeships were set to launch later in the year.

Recent analysis by the Federation of Master Builders showed that the construction sector was facing a shortfall of labour and that it needed an additional 2,200 workers a year in order to meet demand.

Steven Walker, a construction manager with Williams Homes, said it was "really important" that more young people came into the construction industry.

"We have an ageing workforce across the country" he said. "It's really important that young people are being pushed through to be work ready to be the next generation of construction workers".

There was always room for more workers, he mentioned.

"We can always create the space for young people to come and work on our construction sites.

"We buddy them up with an experienced worker, we show them the ropes, we give them the training, we look after them, we interview them regularly to see that they're OK and that they're looked after."

He mentioned that schemes like Academi Adra give young people hands-on experience on the job.

"The classroom-based teaching is really important. It prepares them for the work... and then when they come to us, they'll actually put into practice what they've seen in the classroom.

Adra's chief executive Jones said that it was vital there are enough opportunities in place.

"It's really important that organisations like Adra work in partnership with other organisations to make sure that there are opportunities for young people.

Speaking at one of Adra's developments of over 58 social and affordable homes in Bangor, Jones said additional funding was needed to give more young people opportunities to get into the sector.

"There's a need for a long-term plan, but also a plan is nothing without the funding behind it," he said.

"We need some kind of assurance that there is a long-term plan to support the funding of placements in work, to support young people into employment and to support employers."

Academi Adra scheme was established in 2021 with the aim of providing young people with skills and experience in the workplace, offering courses in construction.

Two-hundred-and-thirty participants have been supported since the launch of the scheme, with the most recent course having 108 applicants for only six positions.

Elin Williams, who oversees the work of the Academi, said that funding had been needed to offer more young people the chance to join similar schemes.

She said: "We've been very lucky to be able to have some external grant funding to allow us to run some courses and pay for placement opportunities.

"We're calling for more funding for opportunities and projects like Academi Adra... We want to carry on to develop and expand to meet the rising demand that we're seeing."

In recent months, Welsh figures suggested that the proportion of young people in Wales who are not in education, employment, or training (Neet) has risen sharply.

They increased to 17% and returned to levels last seen around 2013, according to Welsh government figures.

Cian Halliday, 26, a carpenter from Llanrug, had been made redundant during the Covid-19 pandemic, something he said had been "difficult, and a struggle".

"Academi Adra were offering courses, and almost 16 weeks of work experience and at the end they decided to keep me on as a labourer. I did that for a year," he said.

"Then they offered me an apprenticeship and I chose to be a carpenter."

He said that being made redundant had been very tough.

"It was difficult, and a struggle to find work, so I decided, the minute this opportunity came up, to start a new job."

While looking for work, Cian said that there had not been enough opportunities for young people like him.

"I was happy enough to change careers. I jumped at the opportunity and never looked back," he said.

Daniella Williams, 35 also got into the construction industry after a period of not being in work following an illness.

"I used to work within the NHS. I had problems with my health and I had children, so I left that job, and I really wanted to get into an office based job", she said.

Williams followed a course with Academi Adra to get into an administrative role.

"It's changed mine and my children's lives... I've been able to save, I've bought my own car, and it's given me so much more confidence," she said.

"I've been able to achieve so much that I wasn't able to achieve before, and it's inspired my children as well to go on and do bigger and better than myself as well."

Williams said she was also passionate about helping inspire young girls to follow careers in the construction industry.

"'I work with schools... especially to get girls into construction.

"It's not just bricks and building, there are all kinds of different things. We work a lot with local companies, and it's a great sector to get into, I really enjoy it."

Local colleges had also seen a rise in demand.

Aled Jones-Griffith, CEO of Grŵp Llandrillo Menai, said there had been a "significant growth" in the number of young people who had undertaken construction.

He said: "Our enrolment has increased by 28% since 2025-26 to a record 461 learners this year.

"To meet this demand, we have invested significantly in redeveloping our workshops, recruiting additional staff and buying additional course resources.

"However moving forwards, we need additional funding to maintain this high level of provision and effectively minimise Neets in our community."

'It's about health, jobs and opportunity'

With the rise in demand for homes to be built, CHC said that opportunities needed to be made to end the "housing emergency".

Clarissa Corbisiero, deputy chief executive at CHC, said: "Investing in our homes is the best investment we can make in Wales' economic health.

"In building 20,000 new social homes over the next four years, housing associations can deliver over 14,000 jobs per year during construction.

"By aligning our housing goals with a bold construction skills strategy, we can turn a national emergency into a wave of opportunity for every community.

"Ending the housing emergency is more than bricks and mortar - it's about health, jobs, and opportunity."

The Welsh government said: "We are committed to developing a Welsh skills system fit for the future. Work is already under way to boost construction skills with Level 2 apprenticeships in bricklaying, site carpentry, scaffolding and building maintenance set to launch later this year.

"Construction will also be included in new VCSE qualifications from September 2027.

"A skills audit is currently under way to provide a clear, cross government view of current and future workforce needs across Wales.

"A future Skills Summit is being held this October that will bring together employers, educators, training providers and policymakers to help shape reforms to vocational skills training in Wales."

articles.title: Peace talks rich in symbolism but differences between Russia and Ukraine remain
articles.summary: Despite talks between US envoys and both Putin and Zelensky, the expectation in Kyiv is the fighting will continue, writes James Landale.
articles.body:
The talks in Kyiv were rich in symbolism. The sight of Donald Trump's envoys setting foot on Ukrainian soil for the first time since Russia's full-scale invasion.

The fact they had to travel by train because they could not risk flying and running the gauntlet of Russian drones - weapons launched on the orders of the man at whose table they sat in the Kremlin only hours ago.

The symbolism of Ukrainian President Zelensky greeting Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner at Kyiv's Saint Sophia Cathedral, not only an icon of Ukraine's ancient history, but also just a few yards from where Russian drones hit the headquarters of the country's security services on Friday.

You did not have to join too many dots to work out the point Zelensky was making.

Both sides held talks for several hours; they were later joined by some European national security advisers, including the UK's National Security Adviser Jonathan Powell.

And afterwards, all sides spoke warmly of having held substantive discussions. They spoke hopefully of reviving past "trilateral talks" involving both the US and Europe.

But fundamental differences remain. The US envoys had come hot foot from Moscow where Vladimir Putin had told them Russia was making "tangible advances" on the battlefield.

The story they heard from Ukraine was different, in fact the opposite. Ukrainian officials claim that in August they gained more territory than they lost and Russia suffered 42,000 casualties, dead or wounded.

Putin had also told the US envoys the root causes of the conflict had to be addressed, shorthand for his longstanding strategic demands that Ukraine cede territory, abandon hopes of joining Nato and reduce the size of its army.

After the talks, Zelensky insisted Ukraine would require "strong and clear" security guarantees, including a strong army. Nor did he give any sign of being willing to give up any territory in the eastern Donbas region, an issue he described dryly as "difficult".

Witkoff insisted progress had been made and the ingredients for a settlement were there.

But he admitted both sides would have to make compromises to narrow the differences between them. And right now, it is hard to see either side doing that.

So for now, the expectation in Kyiv is that the fighting will continue and they will face a hard winter ahead.

Some diplomats talk of a window of opportunity for a possible settlement next spring. Others are less optimistic.

Zelensky thanked the US envoys for their visit because the short-term pause in air strikes agreed by both sides had given the people of Kyiv a brief respite. Few expect it to last for long.

articles.title: At least 10 killed in central Mexico fireworks blast during festival
articles.summary: Local government says at least 60 were wounded in the blast, apparently caused by a burning bull effigy.
articles.body:
At least 10 people have been killed and at least 60 wounded in Mexico when fireworks detonated during a village festival, according to the local government.

Video showed revellers carrying a bull made of straw, with fireworks spouting out of the effigy in Santa Maria Canchesda in the Temascalcingo municipality in central Mexico. The AFP news agency reported that the celebration on Saturday was part of a local ritual.

The burning bull apparently ignited a larger store of fireworks in the village church. The explosion knocked down walls and ignited a fire in the town square, according to the news agency.

Local media reported that some people were trapped under falling debris from the blast.

The diocese of the nearby municipality of Atlacomulco said two priests were injured but are expected to survive.

“We join together in prayer for those who have lost their lives, their families and loved ones, as well as those who were injured and all those who are experiencing moments of pain and worry today,” the diocese said in a statement on social media.

Mexico’s Attorney General’s Office said the cause of the explosion has not been determined and an investigation has opened.

Firework mishaps have previously been deadly in Mexico. In July 2018, an explosion killed 24 people at a fireworks factory in the city of Tultepec, north of Mexico City.

Two years earlier, 42 people died in another fireworks explosion in a market in the city.

Genuinely, just shut the **** up! ... It's every ****ing time, bro. It's something every ****ing time! ... Stop ****ing talking about my dogs like that.”The exchange quickly turned into a direct dispute between Marlon and Banks.Richard Banks shares old messages with Marlon Lundgren GarciaOn September 4, Banks responded to Marlon on X. articles.title: Govt in a tangle over Supreme Court ruling on 'creamy layer'
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The Centre is in a tangle over Supreme Court's landmark judgement on \"creamy layer\" that paved the way for induction in the elite civil ser.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Centre is in a tangle over Supreme Court's landmark judgement on "creamy layer" that paved the way for induction in the elite civil services of OBC candidates who had cleared the examinations over past ten years but were denied appointments.On Aug 25, govt approached the apex court seeking clarification on the Rohit Nathan judgement that laid down that "salary" could not be added to the "income" to determine if a candidate from a PSU background falls in the "creamy layer" - like it is done for OBCs from non-PSU families. Govt, while seeking that it be allowed to go ahead with allocation of service for Civil Services-2025 without implementing the Nathan judgement, also raised questions about the SC's definition of "creamy layer".But barely a week ago, Centre told Central Administrative Tribunal (CAT) that it intended to execute the SC order of March 11. "A decision has been made to implement the decision in terms of the judgement rendered by SC in Union of India vs Rohit Nathan," the ASG told the principal bench of CAT.On Aug 19, CAT was hearing a contempt petition against Centre as an OBC candidate, Basant Singh, had sought that the bench enforce its earlier order for his induction in civil services. His case was similar to those of candidates in whose favour SC delivered the Nathan judgement."It is further submitted by the learned ASG that 56 similarly placed candidates are also being considered along with the applicant," CAT quoted the ASG as submitting. CAT put off the case based on Centre's undertaking that necessary steps were being taken to implement the Nathan judgement.The apparently contradictory stands taken by govt within a week's interval have disappointed OBC candidates who felt the SC judgement in March had ended their wait for induction in civil services.The case pertains to department of personnel and training (DoPT)'s differential implementation of the "creamy layer" criterion for OBCs from a PSU background and others. While, as per 1993 office memorandum, "salary" and "agricultural income" are not included in computing the "income" of a family, DoPT has been taking "salary" into consideration for candidates with parents in PSUs. Govt has cited the absence of "equivalence of posts" - categorising posts in PSUs, banks, universities, etc. as "Group A, B, C, D" - as the source of confusion.But, according to guidelines, while Group A and Group B are ineligible for quotas, others are eligible if their "annual income" does not exceed Rs 8 lakh.After a long wait, following orders by three high courts in support of the candidates, SC ruled in March that "salary" cannot be the criterion for determination of "creamy layer" for any category as per the 1993 judgement and that candidates who have suffered should be inducted in civil services.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1929, Louisiana's Oleander Hotel opened on hurricane-prone Grand Isle; 97 years later, residents raised $400,000 to save the island's last historic hotel and turn it into a museum
articles.summary: US News: On an island shaped by storms, tides and generations of coastal life, one old hotel is getting a chance to tell its story all over again. According to.
articles.body: On an island shaped by storms, tides and generations of coastal life, one old hotel is getting a chance to tell its story all over again. According to an online report by Houma Times, the historic Oleander Hotel on Louisiana's Grand Isle is being restored nearly a century after it first opened its doors. Restore Grand Isle, the organization leading the effort, wants to transform the landmark into the Grand Isle Cultural Center, giving the historic structure a new role as a visitor center, community gathering place and museum, states the online report. The community has already raised about $400,000 toward saving the building, adds the report. It is reported that the Oleander opened in 1929, becoming part of Grand Isle's history as the island developed as a coastal resort community. Over the decades, Grand Isle became known for its fishing and maritime traditions as well as its unique coastal environment. The Oleander remained a tangible connection to that past, but years of exposure to the harsh Gulf Coast environment left the historic building in need of significant rehabilitation. Restore Grand Isle has now completed initial stabilization work, an important step toward protecting the structure while plans for its future take shape.A new life for the OleanderThe organization is developing a comprehensive master plan that will determine how the building can be restored, adapted and maintained over the long term. The proposed Grand Isle Cultural Center would combine preservation with public use. Exhibits would explore the island's fishing and maritime heritage, its history as a destination for visitors and the natural environment that surrounds it. The restored building could also host educational programs, community meetings, cultural events and other activities. Rather than preserving the Oleander simply as an old building, the project aims to make it an active part of island life.Community support remains crucialWhile stabilization has been completed, substantial work remains before the Oleander can open as a public cultural center. Restore Grand Isle is seeking additional support from residents, businesses, visitors and people with connections to the island. Donations will help fund continued restoration and rehabilitation while moving the cultural-center plans toward reality. The fundraising effort follows the community's earlier success in raising roughly $400,000, demonstrating the local interest in preserving the landmark.Preserving Grand Isle's identityFor Grand Isle, the project represents more than the rehabilitation of a historic structure. The Oleander offers a physical link to generations of island residents and visitors who helped shape the community. Its proposed transformation would allow that history to remain part of Grand Isle's future. If the restoration succeeds, the nearly century-old hotel could once again welcome people through its doors, this time not simply as guests of a coastal resort, but as visitors learning about the people, culture and natural landscape that make Grand Isle unique.Image Courtesy: Houma TimesCatch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 102-year-old Elaine Keesing and her late husband built their three-bedroom Perth home for about $3,080 in 1956 on land that cost £50-£100; after 70 years, she sells it and prepares for aged care
articles.summary: Rest of World News: Elaine Keesing is saying goodbye to the only home she has ever owned, seven decades after she and her late husband built the three-bedroom property fo.
articles.body: Elaine Keesing is saying goodbye to the only home she has ever owned, seven decades after she and her late husband built the three-bedroom property for about $3,080. Now 102, the Perth centenarian has sold the Salter Point home after living there since 1956 and is preparing to move into aged care.Keesing recently sold the house in Salter Point, a suburb of Perth, Australia, according to real estate website Domain. She and her husband bought a vacant block and built the home themselves after the Second World War, when they had been living in far more modest conditions.In a video interview with PerthNow, Keesing recalled how special it was to finally have a home of their own.“We built the house. We bought a vacant block,” she said, recalling that the land cost between £50 and £100 at the time.“After the war, we’d only lived like in a room virtually,” Keesing said. “And it was just so lovely to come to a home where you had your own bathroom and a lot of space.”She described the neighborhood in those early years as being almost like a country town, where families knew one another and their children attended kindergarten and school together.Home attracted buyers within two weeksKeesing has not publicly disclosed how much she received from the sale. However, Domain reported that the most recent home to sell in the same neighborhood fetched about $2.4 million.The property attracted several interested buyers and went under contract just two weeks after being listed.“The selling process itself was quite straightforward, and we completed it just before the recent downturn in prices,” Keesing told Domain.However, clearing out seven decades of memories proved far more difficult.“The most challenging part was having only three weeks to clear out 70 years’ worth of mementos, papers, family history and furniture,” she said.“It was a bit of a nightmare for my family, but they managed it in the end,” she added.‘I accept that there comes a time to move on’While leaving the house is understandably emotional, Keesing said she has accepted that it is time for the next chapter of her life.“I am a practical person, and I accept that there comes a time to move on,” she explained. “This next chapter will give me a little more support and will also give more freedom to the family who have cared for me so wonderfully over the years.”She said one of the things she would miss most was the garden surrounding the property.“I will miss the large garden surrounding the house,” Keesing said. “It has been a constant pleasure, changing with the years and with every season.”In her PerthNow interview, she also reflected on the memories created inside the house, particularly in the family room, where her grandchildren would gather around the fireplace during winter.“That was their place,” she recalled, describing how her grandchildren would sit together near the step.Her secret to longevity? Eggs and brandyKeesing’s age and independence have made the sale particularly memorable for the real estate agent who handled it.Cristina Spinella of Ray White South Perth told Domain that working with the centenarian was one of the most memorable sales of her career.“When I met Elaine, I couldn’t believe how sharp she was,” Spinella said. “She went into it with a level of confidence, saying she was going to become a multimillionaire. And she was determined to sign the contract herself.”Spinella also asked Keesing about her secret to living such a long life. Her answer was characteristically simple.“I drink brandy and dry every day at 5pm and every day I eat two eggs on toast,” Keesing told her.In the PerthNow interview, Keesing similarly joked that her routine involved a poached egg in the morning and a brandy at 5pm.Keesing hopes the next owners create happy memoriesDespite leaving behind the house where she spent 70 years, Keesing said she hopes its next owners will experience the same happiness she and her family did.“I just hope they have as happier a time as what we had in the house,” she said. “And I hope they get a lot of pleasure from it.”“I can only think of people being happy here,” she added.After seven decades in the same place, Keesing is now moving forward with gratitude for the life she built there, and with the hope that the home will continue to create memories for its next family.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Relief in Congress as all factions accept Pilot as Punjab handler
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: Faced with turmoil over the state leadership in Punjab, Congress has heaved a sigh of relief as politicians cutting across factional lines .
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Faced with turmoil over the state leadership in Punjab, Congress has heaved a sigh of relief as politicians cutting across factional lines have welcomed Sachin Pilot's appointment as party incharge of the poll-bound state in place of Bhupesh Baghel.Former Punjab chief minister Charanjit Channi and Lok Sabha MP Sukhjinder Randhawa, who lead the dissident group gunning for state president Amarinder Singh Raja Warring, extended their best wishes to Pilot. Warring too has welcomed Pilot's appointment.While Channi expressed his "heartfelt thanks" to the Congress brass for "this important decision", Randhawa wished Pilot the "very best for this important responsibility" and said his experience, leadership and connect with the people will give new strength and momentum to the Congress organisation in the state.The duo's first reaction has assured the leadership that the decision on Pilot is in the right direction, though many believe coming days will decide if they are ready to move on from their demand for Warring's ejection. Sources said there is very little likelihood of a change in the state leadership now.Two months ago, Congress was shocked by the outbreak of dissidence in Punjab that goes to polls in February and where the ruling AAP has already launched its campaign for re-election. Congress had announced its election-related committees on July 1, but they have proved a non-starter as the appointments were followed by open groupism that brought the party activities to a halt.Now, Congress is hoping for a new start. The party is planning a statewide yatra in Punjab that will feature Rahul Gandhi, and it may be held towards the end of Sept or early Oct. The schedule will have to take care of the festivals falling in between.Congress hopes removal of Baghel, who had become another target for the dissidents as he strongly opposed their demand to replace Warring, would settle the flux, and allow the party to kickstart its outreach to people.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Inside Taylor Townsend’s emotional journey from adversity to another US Open run, shaped by motherhood and resilience
articles.summary: US Streamers News: Taylor Townsend’s 2026 US Open run ended with a 6-4, 6-3 loss to World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka, but the American still leaves New York with another stro.
articles.body: Taylor Townsend’s 2026 US Open run ended with a 6-4, 6-3 loss to World No. 1 Aryna Sabalenka, but the American still leaves New York with another strong singles showing. The 30-year-old reached the fourth round for the second straight year after beating Diana Shnaider in three sets. Before facing Sabalenka, Townsend had also produced one of the best serving performances of her career, winning all 23 first-serve points against Taylah Preston. Her latest run is another part of a career shaped by setbacks, motherhood and a major rise in doubles.Taylor Townsend built a different path after becoming a motherTownsend’s career has never followed a simple route. She made headlines as a teenager, but her progress was affected by difficult experiences away from the court. She has also spoken about problems involving her early earnings and how those experiences changed the way she handled her career.Motherhood later became another major part of her story. Townsend gave birth to her son, Adyn Aubrey, in March 2021 and returned to competition the following year. Since then, she has continued to compete at the highest level while balancing professional tennis with raising her son.Rather than seeing motherhood as the end of her career, Townsend has treated it as part of her motivation. She has also spoken about wanting her son to have a different experience from some of the things she went through as a child.Her doubles career has been especially successful. Townsend became the WTA’s No. 1 doubles player in July 2025 and has won five doubles titles, including Grand Slam success. She is currently No. 2 in the doubles rankings and is coached by Roger Tyzzer.That success has helped Townsend build confidence in singles too. At this year’s US Open, her serve became one of the biggest strengths of her game. Against Preston, she won every point behind her first serve and hit eight aces. Afterward, she joked about whether she had become a “servebot.”“I don’t know. I think they call this a ‘servebot.’ Am I a servebot now? Maybe.”She then credited Reilly Opelka with helping popularize the term among tennis fans.Taylor Townsend continues to write her own tennis storyTownsend’s fourth-round appearance also added to a growing list of memorable US Open moments. She famously defeated then-World No. 4 Simona Halep at the 2019 tournament and reached the fourth round again this year after beating Shnaider 6-2, 6-7(3), 6-3.Against Sabalenka, Townsend had to deal with a completely different challenge. The defending champion and world No. 1 used her power and consistency to win in straight sets and move into the quarterfinals.Still, Townsend’s tournament showed how far her singles game has come. Her aggressive return position, left-handed serve and willingness to move forward make her uncomfortable for opponents, while her doubles experience has given her another advantage at the net.The result against Sabalenka ended this year’s singles campaign in New York, but it did not erase what Townsend had already achieved. She reached the fourth round at a Grand Slam again while continuing to compete as one of the world’s best doubles players.For Townsend, that is another step in a career she has built on her own terms. Her story now includes elite doubles success, motherhood and a renewed singles run - all after years in which many people were unsure where her career would go.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: 5 poll-bound states set to vote in February-March
articles.summary: India News: NEW DELHI: The advancement of Census in the four poll-bound states of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab and Goa - coupled with deferment of first pha.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The advancement of Census in the four poll-bound states of Uttar Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Punjab and Goa - coupled with deferment of first phase of Census in the fifth poll-bound state of Manipur - has essentially cemented the schedule for the next round of assembly elections in the five states to Feb-March next year.Among the five states, the term of the Manipur assembly is expiring the earliest - on March 13, 2027. The term of Goa assembly ends March 14, 2027; Punjab assembly on March 16; Uttarakhand on March 28; and Uttar Pradesh only on May 22. All five had gone to polls together in 2022, but the first sitting of the UP assembly was on May 22, 2022.Since 2027 polls in these states will also be simultaneous, Election Commission is likely to take the conventional route of winding up polls before the earliest assembly expiry date - March 13.UP will vote almost 2 months before House term expiresThus, the UP polls would be held almost two months before the date of expiry of its assembly. This is in keeping with the pattern of the last three polls. EC's constitutional mandate allows it to hold a state poll anytime within six months prior to the expiry of its assembly's term.Given that a large and populous state like UP is almost certain to have multi-phase polling - though with fewer phases, going by the precedent set by EC in Bihar and West Bengal - polling could start in Feb or even in the beginning of March in case EC decides to restrict polls to two phases, like in Bihar. The poll announcement may come in Jan 2027.Since SIR has already been completed in three poll-bound states and is under way in the other two, EC is unlikely to go for annual summary revision there ahead of announcing assembly polls. At the end of SIR, the electorate in UP stood at 13.4 crore (decline of 13.2%), in Goa 10.6 lakh (10.2% less) and in Manipur 19.3 lakh (7.6% fall). The final rolls for Punjab and Uttarakhand will be published over the next couple of months.Centre had yesterday notified its decision to advance the population enumeration phase of Census 2027 in Uttar Pradesh, Punjab, non-snow-bound areas of Uttarakhand and Goa, to the period between Dec 1, 2026, and Jan 4, 2027, with Jan 5 as the reference date. It also notified the deferment of the houselisting phase of Census in Manipur.The advancing of the population enumeration phase in the four other poll-bound states will avert the logistical challenges that would have arisen on account of a clash between the usual timeline for Census and the assembly elections. Both elections and Census rely on the same pool of govt employees - largely teachers - for their conduct.Conventionally, the second phase of Census is held countrywide in Feb, with March 1 as the reference date.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Voters in key midterm races push back on data centers, and the U.S. strikes Iranian oil tankers: Weekend Rundown
articles.summary: Voters in key midterm races push back on data centers, and the U.S. strikes Iranian oil tankers
articles.body: Dawn Vogel, a Republican county supervisor in rural Iowa, doesn’t have a lot in common with the leading democratic socialists in Congress. But on this bit of policy they agree: Data centers are proliferating across the American landscape too fast. Vogel voted earlier this year for a moratorium that temporarily bans data centers from setting up shop in her heavily Republican county, which favored President Donald Trump 63%-35% in 2024. “I don’t think this is a Republican or Democratic issue,” Vogel said on the sidelines of the Iowa State Association of Counties’ annual conference in late August, adding that she hasn’t talked to a single voter at home who wants data centers. An NBC News Decision Desk Poll powered by SurveyMonkey, conducted from Aug. 20 through Sept. 1, found that 69% of respondents oppose the construction of AI data centers in their local area, with 45% saying they “strongly oppose” the idea. They are all at odds with Trump. U.S. strikes 3 Iranian oil tankers, military says The U.S. military said its forces struck three Iranian oil tankers Saturday after Iran launched ballistic missiles toward two Navy ships. A U.S. aircraft carrier and guided missile destroyer evaded multiple attacks by Iran’s Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps and no American personnel were harmed, Central Command said. CENTCOM said U.S. forces retaliated by permanently disabling one crude oil carrier off the coast of Kharg Island and one near Jask. Forces also destroyed a third vessel near the Gulf of Oman. “If you shoot at two of our ships, we will impose an even higher economic cost — taking out three of yours,” CENTCOM’s commander said. “We will not hesitate to defend American forces, and if necessary, destroy Iran’s limited and exposed oil fleet.” Iran’s Foreign Ministry strongly condemned the U.S. strikes, calling them “illegal and aggressive” and accusing Washington of waging a naval blockade and economic war. ‘Meet the Press’ Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., criticized Republican leadership on a number of issues including the Trump administration’s handling of the Ukraine peace process. Kennedy told NBC News’ “Meet the Press” he believes the Trump administration should take a different approach to Russian President Vladimir Putin. The Louisiana Republican also said his party should do something about inflation ahead of the midterm elections but that it’s “not likely.” Rep. Jamie Raskin, D-Md., told “Meet the Press” in a separate interview that Trump has “undoubtedly” committed impeachable offenses but that Democrats would also focus on issues like healthcare if they win back the House. “Everybody on our side understands that impeachment is a critical tool in the toolbox for constitutional self-defense against a president acting like a king, an imperious, lawless, arrogant king,” Raskin said, responding to a question about whether Democrats would move to impeach Trump if they retake the House. Politics in brief Lone Star spending: The Trump-aligned MAGA Inc. super PAC plans to spend $10 million in Texas’ Senate race.Bring the house down: The Kennedy Center renewed its call for the president’s shutdown of the building after part of a ceiling collapsed.Take three: The Trump administration appealed to the Supreme Court again to restrict mail-in voting, days after the first ballots went out. Rescuers in Nepal pull out two more people alive after devastating floods Rescuers in Nepal pulled a man and a woman alive in separate operations Saturday, 10 days after devastating floods hit the country, as teams continued searching for thousands of people still missing. The man, a Chinese national, was rescued from a hydropower tunnel, according to a social media post from the prime minister’s office, bringing to three the number of workers pulled alive from the Trishuli hydropower project. A photo released by Chinese state broadcaster CCTV showed two rescuers carrying the man out of the tunnel. He was undergoing a health assessment, the army said. In flood-hit Nuwakot, a woman was rescued alive from a house, Nepal’s army spokesperson said. She was airlifted to Kathmandu for treatment. Images released by the army showed rescuers finding the woman covered in mud inside the damaged house. Five dead after Amazon-branded cargo plane overruns runway at Miami airport, striking multiple vehicles Five people are dead and five others were injured when an Amazon-branded cargo plane crashed just outside Miami International Airport on Sunday afternoon, officials said. The Boeing 767-300 cargo aircraft overran the runway while it was landing, according to officials. The plane was arriving from San Juan, Puerto Rico, the Federal Aviation Administration said. Three people are in critical condition and were taken to a trauma center, and two others were taken to a local hospital, according to the Miami-Dade fire chief. U.S. envoys meet with Zelenskyy in Kyiv after peace talks in Moscow U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met with Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy in Kyiv on Sunday, a day after meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow to discuss efforts to end the war in Ukraine. Witkoff and Kushner were greeted by Zelenskyy in Kyiv after arriving in the Ukrainian capital by train from the Polish border, having flown there from Moscow. “Ukraine has always been and will remain constructive. We are interested in bringing the end of the war closer,” Zelenskyy said in a post on X, adding that Ukraine’s “proposals are ready.” Putin, for his part, did not publicly signal any movement from his previous steep demands, which seek major concessions from Ukraine. The renewed talks appear to be Washington’s latest effort to end the nearly five-year war after months of stalled momentum amid the conflict with Iran.
